hello.title: Your clone answers your colleagues first.
hello.body: It learns how you work from your own AI conversations, answers what a colleague asks you the way you would, and brings you only what is yours to decide. On your own, it does your everyday work like an assistant.
hello.fine: 3 minutes · runs on this computer · any step can be skipped

scene.title: What it looks like
scene.askText: Did the payment status values change?
scene.clone: Your clone answers, from your records
scene.cloneText: Yes: 'paid' is now 'succeeded'. From your payments conversations yesterday.
scene.youText: Can you ship it by Thursday?

demo.ask: Can you check the launch copy?
demo.answer: Done: two small fixes in the doc.
demo.decide: Can we promise the client Friday?
demo.question: Sam asks: can we promise the client Friday?

beats.1: Leo's clone brings a request to your desk.
beats.2: Your clone does it the way you would.

beats.5: So that one comes to you: one question, one tap.
beats.6: And the answer is on its way.

firstRun.title: My clone
firstRun.hello: Hi, I'm your clone. To work the way you do, I first need to learn how you work. Here is how I'll learn.

read.title: What I read
read.body: What you asked your AI tools in the last 14 days, your AI instruction and memory files, the kinds of documents and apps you use, and your commits if you write code. For documents I see only the kind, never the contents or names.

keep.title: What I keep
keep.body: Only what will still be true in months — how you work, decide and talk — in five lines or fewer.

skip.title: What I don't keep
skip.body: Things that change, like projects, schedules and files. I look them up when I need them.

time.title: How long
time.body: About 30 seconds. It keeps going if you close this window.

firstRun.folders: These are the folders you worked in lately. Leave out any I shouldn't read.
firstRun.noFolders: I found no AI conversations on this computer. Bringing what your usual AI knows about you is the quickest start.
firstRun.foldersNote: I never read or search these folders. Leaving one out also removes what I had gathered from it for searching.

source.notes: Reading your AI instructions and memory files
source.inputs: Reading what you asked your AI tools lately
source.work: Looking at the kinds of documents and apps you use

firstRun.freshOffer: {count, plural, one {You've had # new conversation with your AI tools since I last read.} other {You've had # new conversations with your AI tools since I last read.}} Shall I see if there's anything new to learn?
firstRun.startOverSure: Move what I remember into a backup and start from the beginning? Nothing is deleted.
firstRun.tryNow: Shall we do one together now?
firstRun.startOverClear: Nothing you taught me is kept yet, only what I read from your records. Clear it and start from the beginning? Reading again brings it back.

import.step2: Paste its answer here. I'll keep only what lasts, and the pasted text is not stored.
import.done: {count, plural, =0 {There was nothing new worth keeping.} one {I kept # line.} other {I kept # lines.}}

flows.intro: What your clone does on its own: at set times, or when a colleague's request comes in. A timed flow's answers go into a conversation of its own.

flows.onRequest: Followed when such a request comes in

messenger.title: On your phone
messenger.intro: Talk with your clone from your phone, in Discord, Telegram or Slack, as you do here. It answers while this app runs on this computer, and what you say there shows here too.
messenger.step2: Paste the token here and connect.

messenger.paired: {bot} talks with {name} only. “/new” in {service, select, telegram {Telegram} slack {Slack} other {Discord}} starts a new conversation.

messenger.taken: This clone already talks with someone else.
messenger.in: You are in. Write here and your clone answers. While you are away from its page, what needs you comes here too.

messenger.orReply: Or reply with your own words.
messenger.waiting: {count, plural, one {# question has} other {# questions have}} waited for you.
messenger.pushNote: While you are not looking at this page, what needs you comes to {service, select, telegram {Telegram} slack {Slack} other {Discord}}: questions about colleagues' requests, your flows' answers, and answers to what you asked. While your status says you are in a meeting, away or off, colleagues' questions wait and come together at 10, 14 and 17.

discord.step1: At Discord's Developer Portal, make a New Application. So nobody else can add it to a server, set Install Link to None on its Installation page and turn off Public Bot on its Bot page. There, press Reset Token and copy the token.
discord.tokenPlaceholder: The token from the Bot page
discord.step3: Add the bot to a server of your own: Discord only delivers a message to a bot you share a server with. A private server made for this is fine.
discord.addBot: Add the bot to a server
discord.step4: Send the bot a direct message, not in the server: on your phone, tap the bot in the server's member list, then Message. A question with a code appears here.

telegram.step1: In Telegram, open @BotFather and send /newbot. Give your bot a name, then a username that ends in “bot”. BotFather answers with its token; copy it.
telegram.step3: On your phone, open the chat with your bot and press Start. A question with a code appears here.
telegram.addBot: Open the chat with the bot
telegram.scan: Or point your phone's camera at this.

slack.step1: At api.slack.com/apps, choose Create New App, then From a manifest. Pick your workspace and paste this manifest; it asks only for what your clone uses.
slack.step2: Under Basic Information, App-Level Tokens: generate one with connections:write. It starts with xapp-.
slack.step3: Under Install App, install it to your workspace and copy the Bot User OAuth Token. It starts with xoxb-.
slack.step4: In Slack, open your app under Apps and write in its Messages tab. A question with a code appears here.
slack.scan: Or point your phone's camera at this.

google.title: Google

steps.preview: With your Google Workspace account, join Google's <link>Workspace Developer Preview Program</link>. Google answers within a couple of days.
steps.apis: <link>Turn on the APIs</link> in a Google Cloud project (pick one or make one): Gmail, Calendar, Drive, Docs and Sheets, with their MCP servers.
steps.branding: In <link>Branding</link>, give the app a name such as sub-office; in <audience>Audience</audience>, choose Internal.
steps.scopes: In <link>Data Access</link>, press Add or remove scopes and paste these where it says Manually add scopes:
steps.client: <link>Create a client</link> of the type Desktop app, then press Download JSON.

google.webClient: A Web application client works too, with this address among its Authorized redirect URIs:
google.typeIt: Or type its client ID and secret

general.aboutBody: sub-office gives everyone on a team a clone: an AI that works like them, does their everyday tasks, and stands in for them with teammates. It runs on your computer, and what it keeps stays here.

ask.body: It asks before it reads a file, opens a web page or uses one of your services. Tick “Don't ask again” on any card to let one kind through.

reads.title: Read on its own
reads.body: It reads files (never in folders you left out), web pages and your connected services without asking. Anything that changes something is still asked.

auto.title: Do it, then tell me
auto.body: It also acts in your connected services and asks colleagues without asking you first. You see everything in the conversation.

preferences.always: Whatever you pick, files leaving your computer, flows, and work in your Claude Code conversations are always shown to you first. Colleagues' requests don't use this: each kind there has its own trust level, under Requests you take.
